text: dsh-workflow-worktree 是供 DSH Web 工作流使用的 Git worktree 隔离适配器。它通过 Cordis patch 插入插件，并向 dynamicWorkflows 注册 isolation adapter；任务开始时按 runId 和 taskId 创建独立分支与检出目录，为子 agent 建立工作目录并记录 lane。任务结束时可保留脏 lane，也可清理干净 lane；另提供 worktree_lanes 工具查看状态。适合需要并行运行工作流任务、避免它们共用主工作区的场景。实现未配置 API 密钥或外部服务，需本机 Git。

dsh-workflow-worktree gives each DSH workflow task a Git branch and worktree, starts a child agent there, and records the lane. A tool reports lane status. Dirty lanes are retained; clean ones can be removed. It suits parallel tasks needing separate workspaces. It requires Git and no API key.
想让 DSH 工作流里的每个写入型子 agent 在独立 Git worktree 中工作。
多个工作流任务并行改代码时，怎样让它们各自在单独的检出目录里运行？
How can each DSH workflow task run in its own Git worktree?
dsh-workflow-worktree 的功能「按任务隔离工作区」：工作流请求 worktree 隔离时，按 runId 与 taskId 创建分支和独立检出，并在该目录启动子 agent；任务结束后依据脏状态保留或移除 lane。

dsh-workflow-worktree README · dsh-workflow-worktree：Git worktree isolation for **DeepSeek Harness workflows** — every write-capable
workflow agent gets its own checkout that cannot touch your working tree, and
survives a crash.

dsh-workflow-worktree README · The gap this fills：[`@dsh-external/workflow`](https://github.com/icetomoyo/dsh_workflow) reserves a
seam for worktree isolation and deliberately ships no implementation. Its README
is explicit: *"worktree 通过 `registerIsolationAdapter()` 接入，未注册时明确失败."*

So a workflow task declaring `isolation: 'worktree'` fails today:

```
workflow worktree isolation requested but no isolation adapter is configured
```

This plugin is that adapter.

dsh-workflow-worktree README · Not another worktree manager：Several plugins manage git worktrees. This one is not for you to use — it is for
the workflow engine to use.

| | manual worktree plugins | dsh-workflow-worktree |
|---|---|---|
| who creates it | you, or the model, on request | the workflow engine, per task |
| bound to | a name you pick | `runId` + `taskId` + session |
| lifetime | permanent until you delete it | the task's, with dirty-lane retention |
| entry point | agent tools / chat commands | `registerIsolationAdapter()` |

dsh-workflow-worktree README · Not another worktree manager：If you want to fork a workspace and keep working in it, use a manual plugin such
as [`dsh-worktree`](https://github.com/FlashingChen/dsh-worktree). If you want
`spawnAgent({ isolation: 'worktree' })` to work, use this one. They coexist.

dsh-workflow-worktree README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @dsh-external/workflow
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-workflow-worktree
```

Then a workflow task can ask for isolation:

```js
await wf.spawnAgent({
  name: 'refactor-auth',
  prompt: '…',
  isolation: 'worktree',      // ← previously a hard failure

dsh-workflow-worktree README · What a lane is：```
<repo>/.dsh-worktrees/wf-<runId>-<taskId>     the checkout
dsh/wf-<runId>-<taskId>                       its branch
<repo>/.dsh-worktrees/lanes.json              the manifest
```

The manifest records `runId`, `taskId`, worktree path, branch, base commit,
session id, and status. Git already knows which worktrees exist; it does not
know which workflow task owned one. That binding is what survives a crash.

Inspect lanes with the `worktree_lanes` tool:

dsh-workflow-worktree README · What a lane is：```
run-7/task-3  dirty
  worktree: /repo/.dsh-worktrees/wf-run-7-task-3
  branch:   dsh/wf-run-7-task-3
  base:     d1015c2e…

dsh-workflow-worktree README · Design commitments：**Never degrade to the shared checkout.** If the directory is not a git working
tree, or the worktree cannot be created, `prepare()` rejects. The engine then
fails the task loudly. An isolation backend that quietly runs the agent in your
tree is worse than one that refuses, because the failure is invisible until the
damage is done.

dsh-workflow-worktree README · Design commitments：**The returned agent is a new agent.** The engine does
`parent = isolation.parent` and reads `cwdOf(parent)` afterwards, so the
returned agent's session must be created *in* the worktree. Returning the
caller's parent unchanged type-checks and silently defeats the whole plugin —
`verify-contract.mjs` asserts this binding directly.

dsh-workflow-worktree README · Design commitments：**Uncommitted work is never discarded.** A lane that still has changes when the
task ends is retained and marked `retained-dirty`, with its path and branch
logged. Git refuses to remove a dirty worktree; so does this.

dsh-workflow-worktree README · Design commitments：**Your `git status` stays clean.** The lane directory is added to
`.git/info/exclude`, not to a tracked `.gitignore` — an isolation backend must
not author changes in the tree it protects. Without this the directory reads as
`?? .dsh-worktrees/` and perturbs the workspace fingerprints workflow
verification takes around each task.

**`dispose()` is idempotent.** The engine calls it on task settle, run failure,
and explicit stop.

dsh-workflow-worktree README · Verified against：`@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.6`, `@dsh-external/workflow@0.1.2`, git 2.47, Node 24,
Windows.

`verify-contract.mjs` runs the adapter against a real repository and asserts the
load-bearing invariants:

```
CONTRACT cwd bound to worktree : true
CONTRACT not the main checkout : true
main tree after agent write    : []
dirty lane retained on dispose : retained-dirty

dsh-workflow-worktree README · Known limitations：- **No merge.** This creates and recovers isolated workspaces; deciding what to
  do with the result is the operator's. Diff/merge-preflight are deliberately
  out of scope for v1.
- **Dirty lanes accumulate.** Retention is the safe default; `recoverLanes()`
  prunes only lanes git no longer knows about, never live ones.
- **One repository per lane.** A task whose cwd is outside the repository root
  is refused rather than isolated somewhere surprising.
